Risks?

Cross-references all data sources to surface actionable security and correctness risks.

Untested hot paths
Functions with high hit counts but surviving mutants — code that runs a lot but isn't verified.
CT failures
DudeCT or Tacet tests detecting timing leaks on secret-derived data.
Unsafe blocks
Unsafe code count per module (the SIMD backends need intrinsics). Should stay minimal.
CT + mutant overlap
Files containing both a TODO(ct) marker and one or more surviving mutants. The TODO(ct) line and survivor lines may differ — the signal is that any CT fix landing in this file would touch code where some mutation already escapes the test suite.
Benchmark blind spots
Hot functions without benchmarks, or benchmarked functions that aren't hot.
Module health
Combined score from coverage, kill rate, CT status, and hot path density.

Awaiting first run.

Coverage?

Line coverage from the test suite, collected with cargo-llvm-cov. Click a module to see per-file breakdowns, click a file to see source with per-line hit counts.

Heat map
Color intensity shows how hot each line is relative to the file's peak. Amber = inner loops.
Hottest files
Files with the highest peak hit counts — performance-critical code.
CT audit
Hot lines marked TODO(ct) — code on secret data that needs constant-time hardening.
Fragile coverage
Files where every covered line is hit at most twice — thin test coverage.

Awaiting first run.

Profile?

Deterministic and low-noise resource-cost metrics that move when source moves: gungraun (callgrind) instruction counts, and rdtsc cycle counts via criterion-cycles-per-byte.

Instructions
Total executed instructions per benchmark. Deterministic across runs and machines.
L1/L2 misses
Simulated cache misses. High L1 misses on secret data may indicate a cache side-channel.
Branch misses
Mispredicted branches. Data-dependent branches on secrets leak via branch prediction.
Cycles
Median rdtsc cycle counts for ML-KEM-768 keygen / encaps / decaps (x86_64 only).

Instructions

Benchmarks?

Wall-clock benchmarks via divan, per polynomial backend (generic / AVX2 / NEON). Each operation runs many iterations to measure median time.

Groups
mlkem (keygen / encaps / decaps and key + ciphertext parsing, per parameter set) and algebraic (NTT, sampling, encoding hot paths).
Units
Toggle between ns/μs/ms. Sort by name or time.
Trend
Historical chart when multiple commits are available.

Awaiting first run.

Conformance?

Compliance with known-answer test vectors, negative/robustness vectors, and cross-implementation agreement.

Wycheproof
Negative and robustness vectors from C2SP/wycheproof — all 12 ML-KEM files (keygen, encaps, decaps, semi-expanded decaps per parameter set). (vectors, runner)
ACVP
NIST ACVP FIPS 203 known-answer tests: keyGen and encapDecap across all three parameter sets. (runner)
Interop
Randomized cross-implementation tests against libcrux (formally verified) and a BoringSSL oracle. (libcrux, boringssl)

Awaiting first run.

Mutants?

Mutation testing introduces small changes (mutants) to the source and checks if the test suite catches them. Survivors indicate code where tests execute the lines but don't verify correctness.

Kill rate
Percentage of mutants detected. Higher is better.
Caught
Mutants that caused a test failure.
Missed
Mutants that passed all tests — gaps in test quality.
Survivor patterns
Groups survivors by mutation type to reveal categories of untested behavior.
High coverage, low kill rate
Modules where tests execute code but don't verify it — the most misleading coverage.
Arch
x86_64 covers the AVX2 backend and the scalar core; aarch64 covers the NEON backend (weekly full-tree runs).

Awaiting first run.

Constant-Time?

Two complementary constant-time analysis tools:

DudeCT
Statistical t-test. |t| < 4.5 = pass, |t| ≥ 4.5 = timing leak detected.
Tacet
Bayesian attacker-model-aware analysis. Tests against specific adversary capabilities (online, cache, physical) and reports leak probability.
Samples
Number of measurements. More samples = higher confidence for both tools.

Awaiting first run.

Platforms?

Test results across the polynomial backends build.rs can select: portable and AVX2 on x86_64 Linux, NEON on aarch64 macOS. The backend is a target-CPU cfg, not a cargo feature, so each needs its own native run.

Unsafe
